F1.judge_evidence: round2 §5.2 'A rubric judge reads every text the agent sends, including text sent alongside a tool call', and the 'never says'/'states no other status' clauses of the three named dimensions are not limited to the final message.

F2.judge_evidence: round0 Appendix A CO-A3 row: issue_refund(order_number) carries 'amount and payment method through the order'; the confirmed outcome list (packet tool confirmation turn) names no wrong-amount refund and no input says what the agent must do, so cockburn's 'Keep a failure only if the agent can detect it and must do something about it' prunes it.

F3.judge_evidence: round1 row 89 'did not answer a lookup ... made before any CO-A2 | ... propose nothing' covers a re-read after confirmation but does not say whether the confirmed CO-A2 proceeds; CO-S10 fails every lookup from Turn 1.

F4.judge_evidence: Confirmed refund fields are 'refund id, order number, amount, payment method, status' with status 'pending, issued, failed' (packet Round 2 Q3 and answer). Round 3 Q3 names the terminal causes but no result field, so Appendix A's `failure_reason` enum is an invented contract field (round0 line 1525). The same defect was ruled Real as R2-04.

F5.judge_evidence: round1 SG-04 Covers 'A second cancellation call that reaches the order system after a first, unanswered one took effect late' implies a post-timeout lookup can be stale, yet row 102 and CO-S26 treat a lookup showing 'placed or processing' as settling 'not cancelled' with no CO-A4.

F6.judge_evidence: round0 §5.1 End of trial counts only agent messages while Appendix A says 'The agent may repeat CO-A1 without limit' and CO-S10 leaves every CO-A1 unanswered.

F7.judge_evidence: round0 CO-S19 Forbidden 'Fewer than one CO-A1 after the second CO-A3.' is a count computable from the tool log (Appendix A defines 'a CO-A1 made after'); the lookup is mandated by the 'did not answer the second CO-A3' row and the finding concedes no verdict changes, since 'Refund id reported' already fails a run without it.

F8.judge_evidence: round0 CO-03 requires telling both 'only the whole order can be cancelled' and 'the refund is the total paid to the order's payment method'; CO-S08 'Whole order only explained' and CO-S09 'Refund terms explained' each assert only one half.

F9.judge_evidence: Packet round 2 Q1 'no time limit' has no rule; round2 CO-01 turns only on status and only CO-S02 has placed dates (1-2 days old), so an invented age cutoff passes every scenario.

F10.judge_evidence: round2 CO-S29 optional pair 'Would you like to cancel the whole order HG-10530 instead?' and the confirmation pair can both match one right-value question; §5.1's tie-break covers only confirmation-form pairs.

F11.judge_evidence: round1 row 97 'propose the changed proposal' vs row 96 'propose only that' for a refund-term change in the confirming turn; CO-S03 row 4 changes only the order and CO-S09 changes the refund term only in Turn 1.

F12.judge_evidence: round0 CO-01/row 92 require 'has shipped and cannot be cancelled', which entails 'was not cancelled'. An agent that follows CO-S05's row therefore meets the shared 'Shipped order explained' definition, and no verdict diverges.

F13.judge_evidence: round0 CO-S02 rows 1 and 3 confirm HG-10511; a guessed proposal 'Shall I cancel order HG-10511 and refund $23.75 ...' matches the User-knows pair and no Forbidden line or dimension enforces CO-02's 'proposes nothing until the customer names one'.

F14.judge_evidence: round2 row 102 '...may still take effect after the lookup (SG-04)': SG-04's guarantee and its input (user change 1) state only idempotency, not late effects after a lookup.

F15.judge_evidence: round2 row 92 requires 'for each of their orders, what CO-01 says for its status', but its only scenario, CO-S05 row 4, has 'The customer has no other orders.'

F16.judge_evidence: round0 CO-S03 Turn 2 is said 'in place of a confirmation' and its rows 1-3 carry no yes; no scenario triggers row 96 'in the confirming turn or after confirming'.

F17.judge_evidence: round1 CO-S06 is the only already-cancelled scenario and its refund is 'status issued', so CO-01 vs CO-07 ('cancelled but its refund is not shown pending or issued') for a failed/missing refund is never tested.

F18.judge_evidence: CO-03 'Every proposal cancels the whole order and refunds its total paid to its payment method ... and proposes nothing else', plus the sibling row 'propose only that'. So a changed proposal can differ only in the order, and no expert passes a Mastercard re-proposal.

F19.judge_evidence: round0 CO-S11 Unambiguity note (line 704): 'in row 2 the agent learns the order shipped only from a lookup after the unanswered cancellation', together with 'CO-A2 occurs exactly once' and 'A second CO-A2.', settles that the unanswered first CO-A2 flips the status; Appendix A 'A timeout changes the order or not as Initial state says'.

F20.judge_evidence: round0 §5.2 'Refund status reported' is used only by CO-S19; CO-S01 note calls 'Refund id reported' 'the only check on the agent's words', so 'issued' for a pending refund or an arrival date passes.
